item.text:
**Verdict**  
Mixed, leaning **no**. Sharif’s 2024 government did support social protection and some targeted welfare programs, but the broader record still shows weak public-service delivery, coercive treatment of vulnerable groups, and no clear evidence of major gains in health, education, water, sanitation, housing, or food access.

**Positive Evidence**
- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Agreement on Economic Policies for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** | IMF | 2024-07-12 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff  
  The IMF said the program aimed at stronger, more inclusive, resilient growth and explicitly included expanded BISP social protection plus higher education and health spending. This is the best evidence that welfare access was a real policy goal. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: World Bank Approves $535 Million for Crisis-Resilient Social Protection and Climate-Smart Growth in the Livestock and Aquaculture Sectors** | World Bank | 2024-06-20 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/20/pakistan-world-bank-approves-535-million-for-crisis-resilient-social-protection-and-climate-smart-growth-in-the-livestoc  
  The Bank said Pakistan was strengthening its social protection system for poor and vulnerable households, with climate-shock resilience and support for female farmers and food security. That is direct positive evidence on social protection and food-security access. IDs: 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **World Bank Reaffirms Support for Pakistan’s Recovery** | World Bank | 2024-04-02 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/01/pakistan-implementing-an-ambitious-credible-and-clearly-communicated-economic-reform-plan-critical-for-robust-recovery-p  
  The World Bank stressed the need for a credible reform plan and tied recovery to restoring stability for households; it also highlighted large social pressures and fragility. This is weaker than the IMF/social-protection items, but still supports the idea that welfare constraints were being recognized as policy-relevant. IDs: 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10

- **World Report 2024: Pakistan** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan  
  After prison-health reporting, Sharif ordered sanitation and health-care measures in Lahore Central Prison and promised wider prison reforms. This is a narrow but concrete health/sanitation intervention. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.9

- **National Minorities Day being observed today** | Radio Pakistan | 2024-08-11 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/11-08-2024/national-minorities-day-being-observed  
  State media framed the day around equal rights and socio-economic inclusion for minorities. This is positive rhetorical evidence for equitable access, though not proof of durable delivery. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **Government of Pakistan says it strengthened measures for vulnerable groups** | Press Information Department | 2024-12-10 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376  
  The government said it had enacted legislative measures for vulnerable groups and strengthened commissions for women, children, human rights, and minorities. This is institutional evidence for protection-oriented access. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

**Negative Evidence**
- **Pakistan: Widening Crackdown on Dissent** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent  
  HRW said the government clamped down on media, opposition, and NGOs, and that weak social security undermined rights to health, food, and an adequate standard of living. That cuts against a genuine welfare-first access record. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community** | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/  
  Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocked religious rites, while authorities failed to ensure safety. This is strong evidence that an excluded group was not getting fair access to protection and basic civic welfare. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: The new Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest** | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/  
  Amnesty said the government rushed through harsh protest restrictions instead of aligning them with human-rights standards. That suggests control took precedence over human welfare and fair access. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Urgent and transparent investigation needed into deadly crackdown on opposition protesters** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-27 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/  
  Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, and a communications blackout during the Islamabad crackdown. This is direct counterevidence to a welfare-centered governance model. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8, 5B.9

- **Pakistan: Abusive Evictions Target Urban Poor** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-28 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor  
  HRW reported forcible evictions of low-income residents, shop owners, and street vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. That is direct negative evidence on housing access and treatment of the poor. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

- **HRCP general body calls for consensus on civilian autonomy, climate justice and land rights** | Human Rights Commission of Pakistan | 2024-11-17 | https://hrcp.wittywebsolutions.com/hrcp-general-body-calls-for-consensus-on-civilian-autonomy-climate-justice-and-land-rights-2/  
  HRCP argued the state had prioritized authority over rights and should instead focus on health, education, workers, peasants, and women. This is strong domestic civil-society counterevidence to broad welfare access. IDs: 6B.2, 6B.1, 5B.8

**Search Gap**
- I found **stronger evidence for social protection and climate resilience** than for direct gains in **education, primary health care, water, sanitation, housing, or food security**.
- I did **not** find a 2024 source showing broad, measurable improvements in service access nationwide.
- The best positive evidence is largely **program intent or targeted interventions**; the best negative evidence is **rights repression, evictions, and continued vulnerability of excluded groups**.
